1.explanation:
We render three instances of the Carbon v10 React Dropdown with the same titleText and helperText to cover the valid, disabled, and invalid states.  

• The first Dropdown shows the default styling and triggers a contrast violation on the gray helper/title text.  
• The disabled Dropdown turns the label and helper to disabled‐gray (contrast fail) and uses the default aria-label "Open menu," which does not match the visible label text.  
• The invalid Dropdown adds the invalidText message under the field (also low‐contrast) and an error icon, which similarly fails contrast checks.  

By running the IBM DAP ruleset in Chrome DevTools on this page, you will reproduce exactly the same violations shown in the bug report screenshots.
1.bug_scenario:
There are three accessibility violations in the standard Carbon React Dropdown component when rendered with a titleText, helperText, and items:

1. Default (valid) state:
   • The helper and title text are rendered in a disabled‐style gray at 12px/400 weight, resulting in a contrast ratio of ~1.71:1, which fails WCAG AA for normal text.

2. Disabled state (disabled={true}):
   • The rendered form label (<label class="bx--label bx--label--disabled">) and helper text are low‐contrast.
   • The <div role="button" … aria-label="Open menu"> on the ListBoxField component does not match the visible label text (“Dropdown menu options”), causing an “Accessible name must match or contain the visible label” error.

3. Invalid state (invalid={true}, invalidText="A valid value is required"):
   • The invalid message and the title/helper are low‐contrast against the background, leading to multiple contrast violations.
